stem: Arrange the following in order of magnitude of work done by the system / on the system at constant temperature : (a) $|w_{reversible}|$ for expansion in infinite stage. (b) $|w_{irreversible}|$ for expansion in single stage. (c) $|w_{reversible}|$ for compression in infinite stage. (d) $|w_{irreversible}|$ for compression in single stage. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

concepts: Reversible and irreversible work in an isothermal process

steps.text: At constant T, reversible expansion and reversible compression between the same states have equal magnitude: $|w_a|=|w_c|=nRT\ln(V_f/V_i)$.
A single-stage irreversible expansion does less work than the reversible path ($b<a$), because $P_{ext}$ is the final low pressure.
A single-stage irreversible compression needs more work than the reversible path ($d>c$), because $P_{ext}$ is the final high pressure. So $d>c=a>b$.

pitfalls: Assuming the irreversible compression and expansion works are equal.

stem: Consider the following chemical equilibrium of the gas phase reaction at a constant temperature : $A(g)\rightleftharpoons B(g)+C(g)$. If $p$ being the total pressure, $K_p$ is the pressure equilibrium constant and $\alpha$ is the degree of dissociation, then which of the following is true at equilibrium ?

concepts: Temperature dependence of thermodynamic quantities for an exothermic reaction

steps.text: $N_2+3H_2\to2NH_3$ has $\Delta H^\theta<0$ and $\Delta S^\theta<0$ (4 mol of gas to 2 mol), and both are nearly constant with T.

$-\Delta H/T$ is positive and falls hyperbolically with T. Also $-\Delta G/T=-\Delta H/T+\Delta S$ lies below it by $|\Delta S|$ and falls with T (it equals $R\ln K$, which decreases for an exothermic reaction).

Option 1 has $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ as negative flat lines and the correct curves for $-\Delta H/T$ and $-\Delta G/T$. Option 3 has positive $\Delta S$, option 4 puts $-\Delta G/T$ above $-\Delta H/T$ and options 2 and 4 draw wrong curves for $\Delta H/T$ and $-\Delta G/T$.

pitfalls: Forgetting that $\Delta S<0$ for the Haber process.

The ion is $Zn^{2+}$ ($d^{10}$), spin-only magnetic moment $=0$ BM.
